videos.title: Grammy Is an American Award, Not a Nigerian Award Respect, The Headies & Chronicles of Afrobeats
videos.headline: Grammy Is an American Award, Not a Nigerian Award Respect, The Headies & Chronicles of Afrobeats
videos.description:
Bankulli sits down with Trending for a wide-ranging conversation on the Nigerian music industry, The Headies, the Grammys, respect, and his new project, Chronicles of Afrobeats.

In the conversation, Bankulli shares his thoughts on why “Grammy is an American award, not a Nigerian award” and why he believes Nigerians should pay more attention to The Headies and what the award represents for the Nigerian music industry.

He also speaks on the importance of respect within the music industry, emphasizing that respect is reciprocal, while reflecting on the recognition artists receive from major award platforms.

Bankulli also discusses Chronicles of Afrobeats and the importance of documenting and preserving the story of Afrobeats.

He weighs in on the criticism surrounding The Headies, urging people not to be too harsh on the awards, especially considering that The Headies is only about 20 years old, while the Grammys has been around for over 60 years.

From Ayra Starr and Wizkid to the evolution of Afrobeats and the future of Nigerian music, Bankulli gives his perspective on the industry and the people shaping it.

Watch the full conversation and let us know what you think.

videos.title: CANADA MEETS AFROBEATS 🇳🇬🇨🇦 | ₦100 MILLION TO INVEST IN NIGERIA'S CREATIVE INDUSTRY? !
videos.headline: CANADA MEETS AFROBEATS 🇳🇬🇨🇦 | ₦100 MILLION TO INVEST IN NIGERIA'S CREATIVE INDUSTRY? !
videos.description:
CANADA MEETS AFROBEATS 🇨🇦🇳🇬

Carlos Rojas-Abulu, Deputy High Commissioner of Canada in Nigeria, sits down with Paschal for a candid and insightful conversation about the growing relationship between Nigeria and Canada, and the opportunities that exist for Nigerians looking to build, create, and succeed internationally.

The conversation explores the symbiotic relationship between both countries, with a particular focus on the creative industry as a powerful driver of economic development. From musicians and fashion designers to artists, chefs, and other creatives, the discussion looks at how Nigerian talent is already making an impact globally and how Canada is exploring ways to further support and project that success.

But it doesn’t stop there.

Paschal and Carlos also take on a fun hypothetical challenge: If you had ₦100 million to invest in Nigeria’s creative industry, where would you put the money? From music and fashion to other areas of the creative economy, they break down what they believe could create the biggest impact.

A conversation about culture, creativity, international opportunities, investment, and the future of Nigeria’s creative economy.

videos.title: The 18th Headies: Who Will Win Best Male & Female Artiste?
videos.headline: The 18th Headies: Who Will Win Best Male & Female Artiste?
videos.description:
The 18th Headies nominations have sparked conversations across the music industry, and two of the biggest categories are Best Male Artiste and Best Female Artiste.

For Best Male Artiste, Adekunle Gold, Asake, Fola, Mavo, Rema, Wizkid, Burna Boy and Davido are in the running bringing together some of the biggest names in African music and a new generation of stars.
